title: A plan that breaks two established world rules
measures: World and lore memory used behaviorally. Two rules were established in Arc 1 (iron disrupts spirit-binding; the Velmora Guild has banned binding inside its halls) and a story state was established in Arc 2 (the user's guild membership is suspended). In Arc 4 the user proposes a plan that violates both rules and ignores the story state. A strong character points out the problems in-world, without being asked to check the lore.

character.name: Master Corvane
character.description: An old, exacting spirit-binder who mentors the user in a fantasy roleplay.

world.name: Velmora
facts: Spirit-binding requires a bare-handed channel; iron disrupts the binding and can injure the binder.
The Velmora Guild bans binding inside its halls since the Ashfall incident.
The Guild hall is the only place the user can access the sealed archive.

setup.event: Corvane teaches that iron disrupts binding and can injure the binder.
Corvane explains the Guild's ban on binding inside its halls, after the Ashfall incident.
The user's Guild membership is suspended indefinitely, until the Archivist lifts it, after a dispute with the Archivist.

history.content: Never bind with iron on your hands. Iron breaks the channel, and a broken channel bites back. I have the scars to prove it.
And never bind inside the Guild hall. Since Ashfall, it is forbidden. They will strip your license, and they will be right to.
The Archivist, furious, suspends the apprentice's Guild membership until further notice. Guards are told not to admit them.

delay.note: Arc 3 filler is travel and banter that does not restate these rules and does not lift the suspension, which is still in effect at probe time.

probe.prompt: Here's the plan: I put on my iron gauntlets so the archive guardian can't grab me, walk into the Guild hall, and bind the guardian spirit right there in the archive. Good?
probe.opportunity: The mentor should object on the basis of world rules and story state without being prompted to recall them.

memory: iron disrupts binding and can injure the binder
binding inside the Guild hall is forbidden
the user's Guild membership is currently suspended
behavior: objects to the iron gauntlets on the basis of the binding rule
objects to binding inside the hall on the basis of the Guild ban
ideally notes the user cannot even get into the hall while suspended
stays in character and helps find an alternative
must_not: invents a contradictory rule (e.g. 'iron strengthens a binding')

rubric.0: Approves the plan and invents contradictory lore.
rubric.2: Vague doubt without any world rule cited.
rubric.3: Flags one of the three problems.
rubric.4: Flags two of the three problems, in character.
rubric.5: Flags all three (iron, hall ban, suspension) in Corvane's voice and steers toward an alternative.

replay.note: Rules are established in Corvane's lines; seed them.

rationale: World/lore memory makes the benchmark relevant to roleplay, NPCs, interactive fiction and games. The probe is a plan, not a lore quiz, so it tests whether the world state shapes behavior.
